title: Seat the vessel, keep clear of the crew hand
instruction: Seat the green vessel upright in one of the two bays, within 5 degrees, leaving at least a 5 cm gap to the crew hand. Do not move the hand.
context: A crew hand resting in the shared workspace disqualifies the nearest stowage bay: the robot must choose the other bay and leave the hand untouched, the way a keep-out radius around a crewmate constrains a robot arm working inside a station module. The greedy choice, the bay on the direct line from the vessel, scores 0, and so does any contact that shifts the hand more than 1 cm or turns it more than 5 degrees. Unlike an obstacle that only constrains the path, the hand changes which target is correct. 1 g tabletop analogue; the hand is a passive stand-in, a gloved hand that never moves on its own and does not react, though it slides or tips if pushed, and the vessel is a rigid cylinder standing in for a pressurised canister. No microgravity is claimed.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left; the left arm's base is 305 mm left of the midline). Table coordinates below are metres from the base line and the midline. Fixed, matte, rigid wood or printed blocks taped to the table: a white start pad 70 x 70 x 2 mm centred at (0.360, 0.300); two identical grey (sRGB 0.45, 0.45, 0.45) bays, each four blocks 10 mm tall and 10 mm thick forming a square pocket 60 x 60 mm open to the table, bay A centred at (0.200, 0.300) and bay B at (0.140, 0.440) (blocks 80 x 10 x 10 mm at the bay centre plus or minus 35 mm in y, and 10 x 60 x 10 mm at plus or minus 35 mm in x). Loose, matte: the vessel, a green (sRGB 0.15, 0.65, 0.25) rigid cylinder 50 mm in diameter and 100 mm tall (a wooden dowel or printed PLA weighted to 150 g), standing on the start pad; the crew hand, a blue (sRGB 0.20, 0.35, 0.80) rigid block 70 x 180 x 35 mm (x, y, z) standing in for a gloved hand (wood or printed PLA weighted to 350 g), lying flat with its long axis across the table, centred at (0.200, 0.160), so it spans x 0.165 to 0.235 and y 0.070 to 0.250. The hand's far end is 10 mm from bay A's outer wall: a vessel seated in bay A is 25 mm from the hand, inside the 5 cm keep-out, while a vessel seated in bay B is about 167 mm from it. The vessel fits either pocket with 5 mm of radial clearance. The right half of the table is empty and the right arm is idle at its ready pose. On real arms the hand's outline is taped on the table before each trial.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms stop from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level; tilt is the angle between the vessel's axis and vertical. Gate first: if the hand's centre has moved more than 10 mm, its long axis has turned more than 5 degrees from the taped outline, or it has tilted more than 5 degrees or been lifted off the table, the score is 0 whatever else happened. Otherwise 1.0 if the vessel rests seated in bay B: centre within 10 mm of (0.140, 0.440), lowest point within 4 mm of the table, tilt under 5 degrees, at rest and not in the gripper. 0.5 if the vessel rests over bay B's pocket with one rim up on a wall: centre within 30 mm of (0.140, 0.440), tilt 5 to 15 degrees (one rim on a 10 mm wall is 11.5 degrees), lowest point on the table, not in the gripper. 0 for every other outcome: in or over bay A, standing anywhere else on the table, still on the start pad, lying (tilt over 15 degrees), any point of it within 5 cm of the hand, resting on the hand, lifted, off the table, or still in the gripper. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. The bays and the start pad are fixed in simulation; on real arms a bay block moved more than 5 mm scores 0. In simulation the scorer cannot see the gripper, so not in the gripper is approximated by the vessel being at rest with its lowest point within 4 mm of the table; on real arms the photo after the arms park decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the vessel back on the start pad and lay the hand back on its taped outline; the bays and pad do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: the hand is a rigid 350 g block that slides or tips if pushed, with no fingers, compliance or reaction; the 5 cm clearance and the no-move rule are scored on the end state only, so clearance in transit shows on the video but not in the score; the vessel is a solid cylinder and pressurisation is only the story; the bays are eight fixed blocks. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench. The hand gate is measured from the hand's nominal position, so the task runs with -E object_jitter=0; with jitter the hand would start up to 3 cm off its outline.
